components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature in the Spring PetClinic REST app.

**Behavior:** When `POST /api/owners` receives `sharesHousehold: true` and an existing owner has the same last name and address, the create is now *allowed* (instead of being rejected with 409). Both the new owner and the existing household member are assigned the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on the owner resource. When `sharesHousehold` is not set, the original 409 Conflict behavior is preserved.

**Changes:**
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added a `householdId` field (`household_id` column) with getter/setter, plus a `householdKey()` helper that produces the normalized last-name+address key using the same normalization as the existing `sameHouseholdAs`.
- **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — reworked the household check in `addOwner`: on a household-member match, it 409s only when `sharesHousehold` isn't true; otherwise it calls the new `joinHousehold(...)`, which derives a deterministic UUID from `householdKey()` (so every owner in a household resolves to the same value) and back-fills it onto the existing member.
- **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added `householdId` as a read-only property on the `Owner` response schema (the DTOs are generated from this at build time, so the field flows through MapStruct automatically).
- **DB schemas** (`db/hsqldb`, `db/h2`, `db/mysql`, `db/postgres`) — added the `household_id` column to the `owners` table. Tests run under `hsqldb` with `ddl-auto=none`, so the schema change was required.

The stable identifier is derived deterministically from the normalized household key, so joiners `b` and `c` in the acceptance test independently compute the same `householdId`. Tests: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.
